merge.reason: targeted re-measurement of the new-YoutubeDL-per-request configuration after the worker mode-flag fix (89e9a62ba); the control was re-measured in the same session so the comparison is internally consistent; the invalid row of the main session is superseded

method.cpu_method: cpu_total_s is the CPU of the whole request tree. For the process-per-request configurations it is the harness getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN) delta, which on Linux is transitive and therefore includes the JavaScript runtime the child spawned. For the persistent workers the worker stays alive, so the worker reports its own getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF) delta plus its getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN) delta; the latter includes the JavaScript runtime it spawned and reaped even though that helper is no longer in /proc.
method.denominators: Every attempt of every request is recorded and every attempt is counted. A retried request contributes all of its attempts to the latency, CPU and memory distributions, so a failure can never be hidden by a later success. The counts are reported as requests and attempts separately.
method.description: Four request models compared against the same videos with the same production resolver flag set; serialized (one request at a time) and interleaved per round so that network and machine drift affect every configuration equally.
method.interleaved: the configuration order is rotated every round

kinds.cold: the first request of a configuration (fresh process or freshly started worker)
kinds.new_video: a later request for a different video in the same worker
kinds.warm_same_video: a later request for the same video in the same worker

probe.method: ranged GET at the head and at the tail with the headers yt-dlp returned
probe.note: the probe always runs outside the measured request window

method.pss_method: Maximum sampled sum of process-tree PSS from /proc/<pid>/smaps_rollup; shared pages are divided between their users. 0 means the kernel does not expose smaps_rollup.
method.rss_method: Maximum sampled sum of process-tree RSS over the whole tree; shared pages may be counted once per mapping process and short-lived spikes may be missed (lower bound).

scenarios.label: challenged video with the default player client (production parity)
challenged video with the explicit web_embedded player client
simple video with the default player client
simple video with the default player client

method.solver_count_method: A shim in front of Bun logs every invocation; invocations that only probe the runtime version (bun --version) are excluded.

wall_definition.fresh_python: process spawn until the response line is read (includes interpreter start-up and import)
wall_definition.frozen_cli: process spawn until process exit (includes interpreter start-up)
wall_definition.persistent_python_*: request written to the worker until the response line is read

method.worker_invalidation_policy: The worker rebuilds the YoutubeDL object whenever the cookie jar, the proxy or the account context changes. The quality preference is applied through a callable format selector, because YoutubeDL.__init__ freezes a string format selector.

workloads.default_client: Production parity. The resolver does not pass a player client, so the default client is used: the challenged video with the default client plus the two unchallenged videos.
workloads.forced_web_embedded: Explicit challenge control: the same challenged video with the web_embedded player client. These numbers are never mixed with the default-client workload.

packaging.note: A persistent Python worker needs a Python runtime plus the yt-dlp and yt-dlp-ejs packages on every target. The frozen yt-dlp executable already bundles its own transient interpreter, the EJS solver package and the extractor registry in one file.

startup_cost_ms.note: The import cost is the same in both variants; the extractor registry is imported by YoutubeDL.__init__ (add_default_info_extractors), so the difference shows up in the construction step. upstream_cache_probe.description: Two frozen-CLI extractions of the challenged video with one shared --cache-dir. The upstream cache holds public signature data; it does not hold n-challenge results.

upstream_sources.fact: YoutubeDL.get_info_extractor caches the extractor instance in _ies_instances, so one YoutubeDL object keeps YoutubeIE._code_cache (player JS) and YoutubeIE._player_cache (n / sigfuncs / sts) across extract_info calls.
upstream_sources.title: yt-dlp 2026.08.19 - yt_dlp/YoutubeDL.py (get_info_extractor, _ies_instances)

upstream_sources.fact: solve_js_challenges() always submits the collected n challenges to the solver; only s/sig challenges consult the cache first (_load_player_data_from_cache('sigfuncs', ..., use_disk_cache=True)). The n result is stored with use_disk_cache=False, i.e. in memory only.
upstream_sources.title: yt-dlp 2026.08.19 - yt_dlp/extractor/youtube/_video.py (solve_js_challenges, _load_player_data_from_cache, _store_player_data_to_cache)

upstream_sources.fact: YoutubeDL.__init__ builds self.format_selector once from params['format']; a callable params['format'] is evaluated per request, so a reused object can still honour a changing quality preference.
upstream_sources.title: yt-dlp 2026.08.19 - yt_dlp/YoutubeDL.py (format_selector, build_format_selector, _select_formats)

upstream_sources.fact: The challenge solver spawns one JavaScript runtime process per bulk_solve call (bun --bun run --no-addons --prefer-offline --no-install -), so a Bun process is started for every extraction that carries an n challenge.
upstream_sources.title: yt-dlp 2026.08.19 - yt_dlp/extractor/youtube/jsc/_builtin/bun.py (_run_js_runtime)

upstream_sources.fact: The upstream lazy_extractors module makes the extractor import lazy; without it, YoutubeDL.__init__ imports every extractor module. The upstream release build generates it with devscripts/make_lazy_extractors.py.
upstream_sources.title: yt-dlp 2026.08.19 - yt_dlp/extractor/extractors.py, devscripts/make_lazy_extractors.py
